title: Spines and right cancellation generate inner horns
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and standard simplices of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and inner horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in fixed universes. For $n\geq2$ let $I_n\subseteq\Delta^n$ be the simplicial subset generated by the edges $[j,j+1]$, $0\leq j<n$. Let $\mathcal A$ be a class of degreewise injective simplicial maps. Suppose it contains all isomorphisms and is closed under composition, pushouts, small coproducts, small continuous transfinite compositions, and retracts of arrows. Use colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; a pushout is the colimit of a span, and a coproduct is the colimit of a discrete diagram. These colimits are computed degreewise in sets. A continuous transfinite composition is the map $Z_0\to Z_\theta$ of a diagram indexed by a small ordinal interval $[0,\theta]$ such that $Z_\beta=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha$ at every nonzero limit ordinal $\beta\leq\theta$; all successor maps must belong to the class. An arrow retract of $g:A'\to B'$ is a map $f:A\to B$ with maps $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $r:A'\to A$, $s:B'\to B$ satisfying $ga=bf$, $fr=sg$, $ra=1_A$, $sb=1_B$.
Assume also right cancellation among monomorphisms: if $u:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $v:B\hookrightarrow C$ satisfy $u\in\mathcal A$ and $vu\in\mathcal A$, then $v\in\mathcal A$. If $I_n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ belongs to $\mathcal A$ for every $n\geq2$, then $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ belongs to $\mathcal A$ for every $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, inner-horn consequence of its mid-anodyne conclusion; saturation as defined in Appendix Definition 7.4. Read online 2026-10-17, not archived; WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this simplicial combinatorial criterion.

proof.text: Use the standard simplex of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a nonempty vertex subset $V\subseteq[n]$, write $\Delta^V$ for the simplicial subset of maps with image in $V$, and $F_j^n=\Delta^{[n]\setminus\{j\}}$. Unions and intersections of these subsets are degreewise unions and intersections: precomposition preserves the condition on images. Every weakly increasing map $[r]\to[n]$ has nonempty image, so all the following identities can be checked on nonempty subsets of vertices. The spine $I_n$ consists of those maps whose image is contained in a consecutive edge. For the auxiliary dimension-one case below, put $I_1=\Delta^1$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: For any two simplicial subsets $U,V$ of a fixed simplex, their union is the pushout $U\amalg_{U\cap V}V$. Indeed two simplicial maps agreeing on $U\cap V$ define a unique map on $U\cup V$ by using the given map on each part; agreement makes it well-defined in every degree and the two simplicial naturality equations imply naturality on the union. This is exactly the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus a union inclusion is a pushout of the inclusion of the intersection into the newly attached part.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: For $m\geq2$ put $E_m=I_m\cup F_m^m$. The intersection $I_m\cap F_m^m$ is the spine on the ordered vertices $0,\ldots,m-1$, hence is $I_{m-1}$ under $F_m^m\cong\Delta^{m-1}$. By step 2, $I_m\hookrightarrow E_m$ is a pushout of $I_{m-1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{m-1}$. This latter map is assumed to belong to $\mathcal A$ when $m>2$; when $m=2$ it is the identity of $\Delta^1$, which belongs to $\mathcal A$. Therefore $I_m\hookrightarrow E_m$ belongs to $\mathcal A$ for all $m\geq2$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: The composite $I_m\hookrightarrow E_m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ is the assumed spine inclusion. Right cancellation applied to this composite and the map established in step 3 gives $E_m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\in\mathcal A$, for every $m\geq2$. All three maps are inclusions of simplicial subsets, hence are monomorphisms, as cancellation requires.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: Put $B_n=F_0^n\cup F_n^n$. For $n=2$, $B_2=I_2$, so $I_2\hookrightarrow B_2\in\mathcal A$. For $n\geq3$, first attach $F_n^n$ as in step 3. For the next attachment, the order-preserving bijection $[n-1]\cong\{1,\ldots,n\}$ identifies $F_0^n\cap I_n$ with $I_{n-1}$ and $F_0^n\cap F_n^n$ with $F_{n-1}^{n-1}$. Thus $F_0^n\cap E_n$ identifies with $E_{n-1}$. Also $E_n\cup F_0^n=B_n$, because each consecutive edge lies in $F_0^n$ or $F_n^n$. Step 2 and step 4 give $E_n\hookrightarrow B_n\in\mathcal A$ by pushout, and composition with step 3 gives $I_n\hookrightarrow B_n\in\mathcal A$. Transport across the displayed order isomorphism uses only composition with isomorphisms, which are in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: We now prove a simultaneous induction claim: for each $n\geq2$ and each nonempty $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, put $L(n,S)=\bigcup_{j\in[n]\setminus S}F_j^n$; the union contains $B_n$ because $0,n\notin S$, and therefore contains $I_n$ by step 5; then both $I_n\hookrightarrow L(n,S)$ and $L(n,S)\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ belong to $\mathcal A$. Induct strongly on $n$. At $n=2$ the only $S$ is $\{1\}$, and $L(2,S)=I_2$, so the two maps are an identity and the assumed spine inclusion. At each larger $n$, prove the first map for all $S$ by induction on $t=(n-1)-|S|$, starting at $t=0$. Once the first map for a given $S$ is proved, right cancellation with $I_n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ proves its second map. These cancellations involve only subset inclusions.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq3$ and assume the whole claim of step 6 for smaller dimensions. When $t=0$, $S=\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $L(n,S)=B_n$. The first map is given by step 5, and its second map follows by the cancellation specified in step 6. This starts the induction on $t$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: For $t>0$, choose $b\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}\setminus S$ and set $T=S\cup\{b\}$. The value of $t$ for $T$ is $t-1$, so the inner induction gives $I_n\hookrightarrow L(n,T)\in\mathcal A$. Since the indices omitted from the union differ exactly by $b$, $L(n,S)=L(n,T)\cup F_b^n$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: Let $d_b:[n-1]\to[n]$ be the increasing injection missing $b$, and let $U=d_b^{-1}(T)=d_b^{-1}(S)$. The face $F_b^n$ is identified with $\Delta^{n-1}$ by $d_b$. Under this identification its intersection with $L(n,T)$ is $L(n-1,U)$. Indeed an $r$-simplex of $F_b^n$ is $d_b\alpha$ for a unique weakly increasing $\alpha:[r]\to[n-1]$. It lies in $L(n,T)$ exactly when its image omits some $j\notin T$; such a $j$ is different from $b$, hence uniquely $j=d_b(a)$ with $a\notin U$. This is precisely the condition that $\alpha$ lie in $L(n-1,U)$. The identification commutes with precomposition, so it is an equality of simplicial subsets, not just of vertices.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: The restriction of $d_b$ gives a bijection from $U$ onto $S$, because $b\notin S$. Hence $U$ is nonempty. Since $0<b<n$, the endpoints of $[n-1]$ map to $0,n$, neither of which lies in $T$. Thus $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-2\}$. Also $n-1\geq2$. These are exactly the hypotheses for the outer induction claim in dimension $n-1$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: The outer induction therefore gives $I_{n-1}\hookrightarrow L(n-1,U)\in\mathcal A$. Cancelling it from its composite $I_{n-1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n-1}\in\mathcal A$ gives $L(n-1,U)\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n-1}\in\mathcal A$. By step 9 and composition with the face isomorphism, this is the inclusion $F_b^n\cap L(n,T)\hookrightarrow F_b^n$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: By the union pushout of step 2, the map in step 11 pushes out to $L(n,T)\hookrightarrow L(n,S)\in\mathcal A$. Composing with step 8 proves $I_n\hookrightarrow L(n,S)\in\mathcal A$. Cancelling this inclusion from the assumed $I_n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\in\mathcal A$ gives $L(n,S)\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\in\mathcal A$. This closes the induction on $t$, and then the induction on $n$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).

proof.text: For $0<i<n$ take $S=\{i\}$. By the horn definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $L(n,\{i\})=\Lambda_i^n$. The second map in the established claim of step 6 is exactly $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, proving the assertion for every $n\geq2$. No outer horn is claimed.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Lemma 3.5, proof (read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED).
